title: Attention
paragraphs: It looks like some adventurers are fighting in the square in front of the Adventurer’s Guild. The spectators include passersby and other adventurers, and in the center of the circle, a fight is currently taking place. One of them looks rough, with a dark complexion, a sturdy build, and a simple-minded vibe—someone who looks like he’d fit in with a bunch of bandits. Is he using his fists as weapons? He’s equipped with knuckles.

The other one looks Japanese. Since there are quite a few descendants of people from another world in this world, it’s not surprising to see someone who looks like that. How old would he be? About the same as Ren or Itsuki, I’d say. He still has a bit of youthful innocence left. He’s wearing light armor and seems to be handling his opponent with just a one-handed sword.
“Hey! Quit running around!”
“…Is this all you’ve got?”
The Japanese-looking one seems to be on the offensive. His level is probably higher.
“Buuu!”
It looks like there are about three pigs cheering for the Japanese-looking one. Three of them… how unpleasant. They remind me of someone.
“This is the end!”
The Japanese-looking one knocked away the knuckles with his sword and used the opening to point his sword at his opponent’s neck. Oh, not killing him is quite an admirable attitude.
“The match is over.”
“Damn…”
The brawny adventurer groaned regretfully.
“Bubububu!”
“Bububu!”

The pigs are making a fuss, acting all triumphant. It’s clear that this isn’t a situation that leaves a good impression. How should I put it… this is triggering my trauma! Specifically, it’s reminding me of the time when I used to chase after pigs and acted the same way with that Crimson Swine.
“H-Hey, is that really you!?”
The brawny adventurer raised his voice in surprise. What’s this now? Is that guy famous or something?
“Father, what did that pig say?”
“She was bragging about something. He’s asking if the guy doesn’t know that he’s become a famous adventurer lately.”
“Hmm…”
“Ooooh!”
A cheer went up. Looks like he’s somewhat well-known.
“Bubu!”
“That’s right!”
“Don’t get cocky just because you’re a little strong!”
“Damn…”

It seems that the brawny one was a notorious adventurer who had been getting too full of himself lately. The people around started siding with the Japanese-looking one. The brawny adventurer left in frustration, as if running away.
“Man, that was satisfying!”
“That guy’s been acting all high and mighty lately, so everyone was fed up with him.”
“Well done!”

Hmm… Since we weren’t here from the start, it’s a bit difficult for us to grasp the situation. However, perhaps trying to act cool, the Japanese-looking adventurer scratched his head in annoyance and walked over to the pigs who seemed to be his companions. Then, he handed over the sword he was holding.
“Ah! The Hero’s party!?”

As I clapped my hands along with the others, one of them noticed us behind them and raised his voice, making way for us. Then, the others followed suit, shrinking back and opening a path for us toward the Japanese-looking adventurer. Why is this happening? We’re not particularly interested in some random adventurer.
“We were just watching…”
“Doesn’t this atmosphere make it feel like we have to go talk to him?”
“Seems like it.”
Father and the others, following the mood, waved as they stepped out of the circle and approached the adventurer.
“You’ve got pretty good skills, don’t you?”

I felt that the Japanese-looking adventurer was giving Ren a suspicious look. Well, it’s not hard to see how Ren’s tone might come off as condescending. This is probably one of the reasons Ren is often misunderstood.
“Ren-san, that attitude is rude right off the bat.”
Itsuki said that to clear up the misunderstanding.

“We are the Four Holy Heroes, and we just happened to stop by and see what was going on. I’m the Bow Hero, Itsuki Kawasumi. This is the Sword Hero, Ren Amaki. Over there is the Shield Hero, Naofumi Iwatani, and that one is the Spear Hero—”
“The Love Hunter! Motoyasu Kitamura, at your service!”
A sudden self-introduction. I made sure to emphasize it so there’s no mistake. While my title is the Spear Hero, my profession is the Love Hunter.
The Japanese-looking adventurer glanced around, giving us a once-over before putting on a faint, practiced smile.
“I’m Yuta Railvatz. Nice to meet you.”
“Bubu!”
“Bububu!”
“Bub!”
The three pigs chimed in as well. Leaving the pigs aside, he seems relatively decent.
“Yuta…? A Japanese name?”
“Iwatani-dono, many parents give their children names like those of the heroes. It’s not unusual.”

Éclair explained the situation. I see, so that’s how it is. Come to think of it, Takt also sounds like a Japanese name. That said, because of this, my impression of this Yuta fellow is absolutely the worst.
“Oh, is that so? I guess it’s like being named after a hero or something?”
“Um… so, what do you want with us?”
The adventurer named Yuta asked cautiously. Ren was the one who answered.
“No, as Itsuki just said, we just happened to come across this commotion. That’s all.”
“Yeah, since the others cleared a path for us, ignoring it felt rude.”
Because of Ren and Itsuki’s words, silence fell over the area. The spectators began murmuring. Father looked at us with a troubled expression.

However, there’s nothing noteworthy to comment on. The most that can be said is what Ren pointed out —that he has decent skills. Indeed, for a mere adventurer, his abilities are relatively good, aren’t they?
But that’s about it. Simply put, he wouldn’t be able to beat Ren. Whether in skill or anything else.

As for Itsuki, he could probably shoot him down from a distance with pinpoint accuracy, and even if I were cornered, I could easily brush him off. Father would probably read his moves and dodge them. If trained, he might reach Éclair’s level, but that’s about it.
“Bububuhi.”
The pig said something.
“Huh? Words of praise? Why? Wasn’t that just a fight?” Father asked with a genuinely puzzled expression.
He tilted his head, looking at me, Ren, and Itsuki for an explanation. But I don’t understand it either. Ren and Itsuki seemed equally confused, unsure how to respond.

To begin with, why should we offer words of praise to someone like him? If being the winner of a fight makes someone great, then I’m the greatest. But that’s not how reality works. It’s those who are intelligent, gentlemanly, and willing to fight for others who deserve praise. I’m striving to become a man worthy of Filo-tan.
“Linelle!”
Yuta, or whatever his name is, stopped the pig.
“Well, we have things to do, so we’ll be going…”
With a business-like smile, Yuta distanced himself from us as if trying to escape. Following his lead, the others around us also began to disperse.
“Did I say something wrong? The woman with him was looking at us like she couldn’t believe what she was seeing…”
“No, I don’t think Naofumi’s reaction was strange.”
“Yes, at least from my perspective, Naofumi-san’s response was the more natural one.”
“I agree with the heroes. I can’t understand what she was thinking when she asked that.”
Same here. What were those people trying to do?
“By the way, didn’t it remind you of a scene from a sports manga where an upperclassman notices the protagonist and starts paying attention to them?”
“Ah, yes, that’s true. It felt like they were trying to force that upperclassman role onto us, didn’t it?”
“I don’t read much manga, but I thought the same.”

Indeed. There was an air of trying to force us to remember them. Unfortunately, he’s not someone worth that much attention. Perhaps the kind of talent that comes along once every three months. Among the slaves in Father’s domain, there were plenty like him. With that level, I’ll probably forget him by tomorrow.
What was his name again? Cola, was it?
“Isn’t it just beating up a disposable character in a predictable position…?”
“And then the women around them started boasting, ‘That’s the famous adventurer Yuta-sama!’ like it was some sort of trump card.”
“A complete textbook scenario.”
“Nano? Is he famous?” Rival asked.
I don’t know. At the very least, across all the loops so far, I have no recollection of anyone named Cola.
